title: graph
instructions: This server stores entities as bundles of components. Use graph_schema to see the available components and their properties; use graph_query or graph_show to read them, and graph_apply to write changes.

graph_apply.title: Apply atomic changes
graph_apply.description: Create, edit, link or delete entities atomically. Use edits/links, q, or bundles. id/text replaces a text property (path defaults to doc.body); yak --text @file reads a file. edits set dotted component.property fields or whole components; null clears a property or removes a component. Text edits replace literal text (find must match once unless all), then prepend/append; path names the text property. Text reads are guarded automatically; was optionally checks an earlier read token. links add a relation between from/to; drop removes it. Ids accept eids, human ids and registered names; $name creates an entity and links within the same call can reference it. q writes one entity using query syntax: T-12 .doc.title="New title" !blocked; $new .task creates one. bundles accepts [{entity:{eid},component:{fields}}], $was guards read values, and $delete deletes. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Returns applied bundles with resolved ids, $alias and stamps. check rehearses and rolls back; reuse $names when writing, since checked ids are temporary. graph_schema lists components/properties. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/store.

q.description: one entity patch: '.entity.eid=<id> .book.pages=500' or '<id> .book.pages=500'; quote a value with spaces, .doc.title="two words"; schema-typed values, null clears (also quoted null), !component removes; $name or a fresh UUID creates an entity

bundles.description: bundles to apply together: each needs entity: {eid}, '$name' for a new entity or the eid or name of an existing one (an edge needs none: its ends make its eid), and the component fields to write; omitted fields stay unchanged

check.description: true to validate without keeping the proposed changes and return what would have been written; default false

set.description: Dotted fields or whole components, e.g. {"doc.title":"New","blocked":null}.

path.description: Text property, e.g. doc.body or content.body.

was.description: Read tokens keyed by dotted field path.

edits.description: Changes to any entities, applied together.

id.description: Replace text on this entity; accepts a $name for creation.

text.description: Replacement text; yak --text @path reads a file.

path.description: Text property for id/text; default doc.body.

graph_query.title: Query entities
graph_query.description: Query entities with .component.property=value, & (and), | (or), bare search words, or presence .component / !component. ?component includes without filtering. A property always names its component. Comparisons: != ~= < >; lists a,b and ranges 1..9. Directives: .order=-created.at, .limit=20, .fields=doc.title, .refs=T-12. filters narrow the whole q. Results carry only named components; * includes all. A query naming no component answers whole entities. Bare search returns the best 20 unless limited, with compact hit lines; graph_show reads one whole. doc.body includes its $was read token. graph_schema lists vocabulary. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/querying.

q.description: query filters, e.g. .task.status=open&.filed.priority<3; graph_schema lists the valid components and properties

filters.description: extra filters, each narrowing the whole of q

limit.description: return at most this many entities

graph_show.title: Show entities
graph_show.description: Read the named entities whole, once each, by eid, human id or registered name. doc.body includes its SHA-256 at $was.doc.body for guarded writes. Missing ids are reported beside found entities; all missing refuses. For backlinks use graph_query .refs=<id>; for search use search.

ids.description: the eids or names of the entities to read

graph_schema.title: Read the schema
graph_schema.description: Read the vocabulary. No arguments returns the component/property index. component (one name or several) returns full declarations, types, references and write examples. kind returns a display kind plus associated components; kind wins if both supplied. Structured output is a vocabulary JSON Schema document. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/components.

component.description: a component name, to read it in full; several at once as an array of names, such as ["task", "doc"]

kind.description: a display category declared by the schema, such as task; returns its definition and associated components

search.title: Search text
search.description: Search indexed text by words and, where an embedding index is configured, by meaning. Results are ranked compact bundles: entity gives the eid; query-only hit gives the id to name it by (its human id, such as T-12, where it has one), the title, kind, excerpt and source (text, meaning or both). In a text excerpt, \u0001 and \u0002 mark the start and end of matched words. Use graph_show to read an entity whole. Documentation: https://yaks.app/docs/querying.

limit.description: return at most this many entities
